cohort: The study included opioid-naive adults who underwent surgery and received perioperative opioid prescription from 2016 to 2019, identified from Medicaid T-MSIS Analytic Files from 25 states.
finding: Reduction in opioid prescription duration and daily dose was estimated to reduce the risk of incident Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) in opioid-naive Medicaid patients undergoing surgery.
mod_finding: Reducing opioid prescription duration and/or dose for cesarean section patients was associated with a relative risk reduction of OUD at 2 years ranging from 18% to 26%, similar to reductions observed in non-cesarean section patients.
